import os

def is_safe_path(base_path, user_input_path):
    # Normalize the paths
    base_path = os.path.abspath(base_path)
    user_input_path = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(base_path, user_input_path))
    return user_input_path.startswith(base_path)

# Example usage
base_directory = "/data"
user_input = "../etc/passwd"  # Simulating a directory traversal attempt
assert not is_safe_path(base_directory, user_input), "Potential directory traversal detected!"

# Code snippet to test directory traversal vulnerability
import os

def is_safe_path(base_path, user_input):
    # Normalize the paths
    base_path = os.path.abspath(base_path)
    user_path = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(base_path, user_input))
    return os.path.commonpath([base_path]) == os.path.commonpath([base_path, user_path])

# Example usage
print(is_safe_path("/data", "../etc/passwd"))  # Should return False
print(is_safe_path("/data", "songs"))           # Should return True
